info.bio: Grupo australiano de rock. Formado en 1980, en la ciudad de Sídney, sus fundadores fueron Peter Koppes (nacido en 1955) y Nick Ward. Con influencias de The Byrds, Pink Floyd y Television entre otros. Su música se creó partiendo de principios rock y fue derivando hacia diversos estilos, entre ellos el Pop Gótico, el Rock Sinfónico, etc. Las amplias atmósferas que creaban con las guitarras los convirtió en un grupo de amplias pretensiones y gran originalidad.

scenes.name: Pop de Australia y Nueva Zelanda
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Australia aporta las elegías neorrománticas de los Go-Betweens, las microsinfonías de The Church, Hunters And Collectors, Midnight Oil, Men At Work, Triffids e INXS. Nueva Zelanda cría una generación de antihéroes que no tiene nada que ver con la ola británica comercial y crea el género de los noventa: el «lo-fi pop». The Clean (como si los Buzzcocks versionaran a Syd Barrett y a la Velvet), Tall Dwarfs, Chills, Bats, This Kind Of Punishment, Jean Paul Sartre Experience, Scorched Earth Policy, Able Tasmans, Verlaines y la figura de Peter Jefferies.

xref.title: The Rosary Murders (1987) – Uncredited Child Actor Appearance as Altar Boy
xref.body: While serving as an altar boy at the Church of the Holy Redeemer in Detroit, the young Jack Gillis (later Jack White) made an uncredited extra appearance in the 1987 film *The Rosary Murders*. He is visible in the film if you know where to look. This early exposure to acting contributed to his later interest in it as an adult, including a role in *Cold Mountain*. "Technically, this makes Jack White a child actor."

xref.title: Church of Kurt Cobain (1996) – Media Hoax Won a Contest to Fool The Oregonian
xref.body: On May 29, 1996, a man calling himself "Reverend Jim Dillon" announced the founding of the Church of Kurt Cobain in Portland, Oregon, using Nirvana song lyrics as liturgy. The story received front-page coverage in *The Oregonian*, was picked up by MTV, and led the ABC Evening News with Peter Jennings. In reality it was a hoax — a local radio station had run a contest to see if listeners could trick *The Oregonian* into printing a fake story, and the winner was a man named Jerry Catel, who became "the Reverend Jim Dillon." His secondary intent was to make a statement about media shallowness and celebrity idolatry. "It was a hoax. The truth is that all this originated with a local radio station which staged a contest to see if listeners could get the Oregonian to print a fake story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Arthur Kane's Difficult Post-Breakup Life
xref.body: Bassist Arthur Kane faced severe challenges after the breakup, moving to Los Angeles where he struggled with alcoholism, experienced a near-fatal fall from a window, and was beaten senseless with a baseball bat by a homeless man, leaving him in a coma; he later became a Mormon in 1989 and worked as a librarian in the church's genealogy center. "Bassist Arthur Kane had a rough time. He moved to Los Angeles where he drank himself into an alcoholic stupor. He was so drunk one time that he fell out of a window, and nearly died."

xref.title: Early Life and Influences
xref.body: Born in Manchester on July 15, 1956, Ian Curtis's father was a police detective, and he had a younger sister named Carol. Raised in Hudsfield, outside Manchester, he sang in the church choir and was an avid reader, delving into Dostoyevsky, Sartre, and other philosophers, as well as literature and poetry, alongside a fascination with military history, particularly Nazi Germany. "Ian was born in Manchester on July 15, 1956. His father was a police detective and he had a younger sister named Carol."

xref.title: Funeral Incidents
xref.body: His funeral was disrupted by a "hysterical fan" known for intentionally ruining public events, who screamed obscenities and threatened to hang himself from the church balcony. "Meanwhile, a hysterical fan showed up, started screaming obscenities and threatened to hang himself from the balcony of the church."

xref.title: LGBTQ+ Activism
xref.body: Dan Reynolds became an outspoken activist for LGBTQ+ rights, despite being a straight, married former Mormon missionary with three children. He heads the LoveLoud foundation and music festival, which has raised over a million dollars for LGBTQ+-related organizations. He openly displays a rainbow flag at shows, even in risky regions like Turkey and Utah, where the Mormon church has differing views, and has prompted statements from the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. "Shortly after the evolve album came out, we started hearing about Dan Reynolds' activism for LGBTQ rights."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Most Famous Mormon in Music
xref.body: Dan Reynolds is considered by some to be the most famous Mormon in music currently, and his activism has put pressure on the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, compelling them to issue statements regarding his public comments and actions. "After all, it is possible that Dan is the most famous Mormon in music right now."

xref.title: Philosophical and Satanic Influences
xref.body: Manson delved deeply into the philosophies of Satanist Aleister Crowley and the writings of Friedrich Nietzsche, and formed a friendship with Anton LaVey, the head of the Church of Satan, in which Manson is also a minister (though he doesn't take this seriously). "Manson himself got deep into the philosophies of Satanist, Alistair Crowley, and the writings of the uncompromising Frederick Nietzsche. He formed a friendship with Anton Leve, the head of the Church of Satan. Now, Manson is actually a minister in that church, but he doesn't take that seriously, just so you know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Priesthood Calling Abandoned for Guitar Amplifier – Jack White's Near-Seminary Life
xref.body: Jack White (born John Anthony Gillis) is the youngest of ten children of Gorman and Theresa Gillis, a devout Catholic couple in Detroit. Both parents worked for the Catholic Archdiocese of Detroit — his mother as a secretary, his father in maintenance. Jack served as an altar boy at the Church of the Holy Redeemer and, following in the footsteps of his six brothers, developed a sense of religious calling. He applied to and was accepted at a seminary in Wisconsin, but had a last-second change of heart when he realized he would not be permitted to bring his new guitar amplifier. He enrolled in public school instead. Had he gone, there would have been no White Stripes, no marriage and divorce to Meg White, and no subsequent marriage to model Karen Elson. "So talk about a decision that changes your life, huh?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Satanism Allegations
xref.body: While Manson has been associated with Satanism, he does not consider himself a spokesperson for it or for any organized religion, viewing his ordination as a minister in the Church of Satan by Anton LaVey as purely honorary with no practical power or meaning. He describes his beliefs as a personal interpretation incorporating diverse influences. "I'm not and never have been a spokesperson for Satanism. It's simply part of what I believe in along with Dr. Seuss, Dr. Hook, Nietzsche, and the Bible. I just have my own interpretation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Transition to Pastoral Work
xref.body: After the breakup of Elastica, Donna Matthews left the music industry and entered the church, becoming a pastor. She dedicates a significant amount of her time to outreach work with the homeless. "Donna Matthews. C2 went into the church, becoming a pastor and works a lot with outreach to the homeless."
